summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Summit Retail through the Console usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Focus on how per-route dashboards surface token-level cost, latency, and model selection, and recommendation paths (batching, cache, quantization). Security questions (KMS, audit logs, SAML) flagged; next steps: pricing, pilot, security deep-dive.
topics: Caching and batching effects on cost/latency
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-05 14:00 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Product) — Aisha Patel (Summit Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Eng Manager), Laura Chen (Security), Ben Torres (Product)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we wanted to show you the Console usage analytics and specifically the per-route dashboards and cost breakdown that a lot of retailers have found helpful. Quick intro from our side, I'm Jordan, AE, Priya is our SE who will run the demo.

[00:18] Aisha: Hey Jordan, thanks. We have Marco and Laura on the line too. We're keen on seeing how you show cost per route — that's been a pain point for us.

[00:25] Jordan: Totally. Priya, over to you.

[00:28] Priya: Cool. I'm going to share my screen — let me know if you can't see it. (brief pause) Can you see the Console?

[00:40] Marco: Yes. Looks good but the text is small on my laptop, you might zoom.

[00:44] Priya: Sure — zooming in. Alright, top level is the Usage Overview, we have token consumption, cost over time, latency percentiles. Jumping into Routes — this is the per-route dashboard. Each route is a logical endpoint you define, we surface requests, tokens in/out, p50/p95 latency, model used, and an estimated cost attribution.

[01:10] Aisha: That estimated cost attribution — is that actual billing or an internal estimate?

[01:14] Priya: Good question. It's an estimate calculated from the token consumption and the costing profile associated with the model variant and infra tier. For hosted customers it's within rounding of the bill — within a few percent — for Dedicated or private you'll map that to your committed cost numbers. There's a note on adjustments if you add autoscaling or burst credits.

[01:35] Marco: How do you handle caching? We have a bunch of prefix reuse in chat flows.

[01:40] Priya: We have automatic prefix/KV cache metrics. See it here under Route Insights — cache hits, cache bytes, and the estimated saved tokens. If a route shows high repeated prefixes, the Console surfaces a caching recommendation like increasing TTL or enabling prefix caching for that route. We also show the cost delta if caching were enabled.

[02:05] Laura: From a security perspective, where do audit logs and who-called-what live? Do audits include token-level traces?

[02:12] Priya: Audit logs are in a separate stream — Console links to them. We redact content by default at token level for hosted, but we provide metadata about who accessed which route, model version, and latency. For private deployments you can keep full transcripts in your VPC and integrate with your SIEM. We have KMS/HSM integrations as well.

[02:36] Jordan: Quick aside — we heard you'd be interested in per-route budget alerts?

[02:40] Aisha: Yes please. We need guardrails.

[02:43] Priya: You can set per-route quotas and alerts. Here in Alerts you see a rule; when a route approaches 80% of daily budget it can trigger an email, webhook, or automatic model fallback to a cheaper variant.

[03:05] Marco: Model fallback — can you show an example?

[03:09] Priya: Sure. In this demo tenant we have a customer support route pinned to 'redwood-rt-medium' but with a fallback to 'redwood-rt-small' if latency spikes or budget threshold reached. We'll trigger a simulated spike. (clicks) You can see the routing policy evaluation and the Console shows historical runs of the fallback and the impact on tokens and cost.

[03:40] Ben: How accurate is the per-token cost estimate when you have batching? Our production has big batching windows.

[03:47] Priya: We model batching by amortizing GPU costs across tokens and requests; the Console has an adjustment factor if you enable continuous batching in the infra config. We also surface a suggested batch size and expected latency tradeoff. There's a recommendation card here "Batching: increase to 8 to reduce unit cost by ~22%" — that's based on your request size distribution.

[04:15] Aisha: Curious about quantization recommendations you mentioned in the deck earlier.

[04:20] Priya: Right, under Optimize we run profiling and suggest quantization levels per model variant. The Console will show projected cost drop and any expected quality delta measured against pre-defined prompts. For many retrieval-augmented or short-chat routes, 8-bit quantization yields big savings with negligible quality loss.

[04:43] Marco: Do you have guardrails for quality regression? We can't roll out quantized models without tests.

[04:48] Priya: Absolutely — integrated eval sets. We let you pin prompt/response pairs and run periodic evals; the Console shows quality drift and flags regressions. You can attach alerts to those evals too.

[05:05] Laura: On compliance — SOC2, ISO. We need attestations and encryption detail.

[05:10] Jordan: We'll share the security pack after this call, includes SOC 2 Type II report, ISO docs, KMS integration guide, and the audit log schema.

[05:18] Laura: Great. Also SSO — can we enforce SCIM provisioning and role-based access?

[05:23] Priya: Yes, SAML/SCIM and RBAC are supported. Console shows team-level roles and route-level permissions. We'll include a sample RBAC mapping in the pack.

[05:35] Aisha: Back to costs — can we slice cost by product area not just route? We have multiple teams using the same endpoint with different product tags.

[05:44] Priya: You can tag routes and requests via metadata headers. The Console supports grouping and cost allocation by tag, workspace, or team. If you send a header x-summit-team: checkout we show the tag breakdown.

[06:02] Marco: Can you export the cost attribution to our internal billing system?

[06:06] Priya: Yes — export CSV or S3 sink. Also webhook or API endpoint for programmatic pulls.

[06:14] Jordan: Quick demo of a drill-down — opening the "Checkout Chat" route. You'll see 30-day trend, tokens in/out, median latency 120ms p95 380ms, and cost per 1k requests about $2.40 in this tenant. Note the cost bar breaking down model compute, infra premium, and caching adjustments.

[06:40] Aisha: That $2.40 — is that with dedup/caching applied?

[06:44] Priya: Yes that's after observed cache hits. We also show a hypothetical "no cache" line so you can see the delta.

[06:52] Marco: Any way to simulate increased traffic to see cost projection?

[06:56] Priya: There's a Projection tool — you provide QPS and route mix and it runs a projection with confidence intervals. It accounts for batching, cache hit rate, and autoscaling policy.

[07:10] Ben: On autoscaling — if we move to Dedicated, do we lose any of this console telemetry?

[07:16] Priya: No, telemetry remains. For Dedicated we show tenant-level capacity reservations and committed throughput; cost attribution will reflect committed contract mapping. For Private (VPC/on-prem) we ship the Console control plane but logs and payloads stay in your network.

[07:32] Aisha: Good. For the pilot we expect to use hosted initially. What would you recommend as pilot scope?

[07:38] Jordan: Typical pilot is 2 weeks, pick 3-5 routes that represent 70% of traffic and include 1 high-cost route. We'll run the baseline, enable caching and batching recommendations, and quantify cost delta and quality drift. Priya will help provision.

[07:54] Marco: About SLA and p95 latency — our cutoff is 500ms for checkout flows.

[07:59] Priya: We can set latency SLOs per route; Console will alert on SLO breaches and show tail-failure traces. We also support automatic fallback to higher-priority region or model if latency spikes.

[08:15] Laura: On data residency — our compliance requires EU data to stay in EU region.

[08:20] Jordan: We support region pinning for routes and model variants. We'll note that in the security pack.

[08:26] Priya: One more feature — per-token cost drill: clicking into a request shows token-level breakdown, embedding costs if you do embed+generate flows, and whether the request hit KV cache. This is helpful for debugging why a single request is expensive.

[08:45] Aisha: Show us an example of a high-cost request.

[08:48] Priya: (clicks) Here's a long conversation with a big context window — you can see the KV cache missed and the model used was a larger variant; tokens-in high, embeddings computed for retrieval. The Console highlights expensive steps and suggests moving retrieval to pre-compute embeddings to reduce runtime embedding calls.

[09:12] Marco: Interesting. How do you handle embedding costs when using hybrid search?

[09:16] Priya: We show embedding compute as a separate line item and allow you to pin embeddings to offline jobs. If you use our vector store integrations, we surface approximate cost savings when pre-computing.

[09:26] Ben: Any docs or spreadsheets that show expected cost per 10k requests for different route mixes?

[09:30] Jordan: Yes we'll send a benchmark spreadsheet and a pilot estimate template — that's part of the next steps.

[09:35] Aisha: On ownership — who will be our day-to-day contact?

[09:39] Jordan: I'll be your AE; Priya will own the pilot delivery. Liam is product and will join on architecture calls.

[09:48] Laura: One more on encryption keys — can we manage keys ourselves?

[09:52] Priya: Yes, customer-managed keys supported for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption and can support HSM for higher controls.

[10:05] Marco: Let's talk costs again — when you show the per-route cost savings from caching/batching, is that conservative? We need conservative estimates for our finance folks.

[10:12] Priya: We provide both observed delta (what happened historically given your traffic) and projected delta based on sampling profiles — the projection uses conservative percentiles by default; you can toggle to optimistic/median scenarios.

[10:28] Jordan: Looks like we're hitting time. Quick recap: we'll send pricing + security pack, Priya will provision a trial tenant and sample dashboards, Summit provides sample traffic for initial pilot, and we'll schedule a security deep-dive. Anything else?

[10:43] Aisha: That covers it. Could we get the pilot scoped by next Wednesday?

[10:48] Jordan: Yes we'll aim for that. Priya will send onboarding checklist.

[10:53] Laura: Please include samples of audit log schema and RBAC mappings.

[10:57] Jordan: Noted. Thanks everyone.

[11:00] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had some mis-heard product names (eg "redwood-rt-medium" sometimes transcribed as "Red wood RT medium"); speaker overlaps and filler words remain. Shared artifacts: pricing spreadsheet link (drive.google.com/drive/fake-pricing-sheet), SOC2 pack (link to secure share), pilot onboarding doc (link to onboarding).
